question: A short electric dipole lies along the x-axis with its center at O. Consider two points at the same distance r from O: P on the axial line (+x) and Q on the equatorial line (+y). Which relation and explanation about the field magnitudes is correct?

options.A: |E(Q)| = |E(P)|, because P and Q are equally distant from both charges.
options.B: |E(Q)| = 0, because contributions from +q and −q cancel exactly on the equatorial line.
options.C: |E(Q)| = (1/2) |E(P)|, because on the axial line the fields from +q and −q are along the same direction and add, while on the equatorial line they oppose and partially cancel.
options.D: |E(Q)| = 2 |E(P)|, because the equatorial point receives contributions from two charges.
